scope: Selected effective EC3 tables 121, 123, and 124. This is a source-to-assertion cell review, not certification of §9.8 or §9.9.
source_method: Primary doc/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.pdf was inspected by physical PDF page and footer, including each table caption and continuation. Table 121 is physical 360–361 (printed 345–346); Table 123 is physical 364–365 (printed 349–350); Table 124 is physical 367–368 (printed 352–353). Physical 368/printed 353 starts Table 125, which is outside this table review. Issue #5 on physical364 amends adjacent FD class-descriptor prose, not Table123 class names; no issue annotation was identified on Table124 pages; nearby #337/#453 on physical 360 concern Table 120 and are not Table 121/124 edits.

features.source_location: Physical 360–361 / printed 345–346. The caption and first four entries (bits 1–4) are on physical 360; the continuation (bits 6, 7, 17, 18, 19) is on physical 361. Adjacent §9.8.2 prose states the 32-bit unsigned integer shape, reserved-zero writer rule, Symbolic/Nonsymbolic interpretation, and ForceBold behavior.

cells.name: FixedPitch
cells.meaning: All glyphs have the same width.

cells.name: Symbolic
cells.meaning: Contains glyphs outside Standard Latin; mutually exclusive with bit 6 in valid writer output.

cells.name: Nonsymbolic
cells.meaning: Uses Standard Latin names/set or subset; mutually exclusive with bit 3 in valid writer output.

cells.name: SmallCap
cells.meaning: Lowercase shapes correspond to uppercase, proportion-adjusted.

cells.name: ForceBold
cells.meaning: The following prose says the processor shall use this flag to determine whether bold glyphs are painted with extra pixels at small sizes; thickening is permitted, not specified as a mandatory pixel kernel.
Reserved and shall be zero in PDF-writer output.

features.ec3_and_errata: No annotation on the Table 121 continuation changes these meanings. #337 and #453 share physical page 360 but their annotation rectangles target Table 120 FontName/MissingWidth material; they do not amend Table 121.
features.implementation_and_assertions: `pdf-font::metrics::descriptor_flags` reads only nonnegative u32-valued integer flags; `truetype::is_symbolic` uses bit 3. `crates/pdf-font/src/truetype_flags_audit.rs::a_conflicting_flags_word_follows_symbolic_with_route_controls` has independently distinct MacRoman and Unicode cmap routes and asserts Symbolic-only, Nonsymbolic-only, and contradictory-bits behavior. This tests the §9.6.5.4 code-table consequence, not every Table 121 flag. `substitute::Style::derive` consumes FixedPitch/Serif/Italic/ForceBold as substitute style; several family-selection assertions are environment-gated. `rich_text::layout` uses Italic and ForceBold for constructed appearance style. Current durable descriptor shard `font_descriptor_cells_current` maps word bounds, invalid-type controls, contradictory flags and substitute consumers; its source reading treats zeroing of reserved bits as a writer rule and small-size thickening as underdetermined by the spec's permitted effect wording.
features.verdict: Selected semantic consumers are tested. The symbolic precedence control is strong for the one reader recommendation the prose actually gives. No all-bits raster matrix is implied, and no pixel-exact ForceBold requirement was derived.
features.residuals: This shard does not test each style bit's raster consequence, all valid/reserved-bit combinations, or a ForceBold small-device raster. Such behavior was not promoted as a defect: the source leaves whether to thicken at small sizes open and states no kernel or threshold. Font substitution ranking is also product policy.

features.table: Table 123 — Glyph classes in CJK fonts
features.source_location: Physical 364–365 / printed 349–350. The caption and Adobe-GB1/Adobe-CNS1 rows start physical 364; Adobe-Japan1/Adobe-Japan2/Adobe-Korea1/Adobe-KR rows continue on physical 365. §9.8.3.3 introduces that class names depend on Registry, Ordering, and Supplement; Table 123 supplies the collection-specific names and descriptions.
features.ec3_and_errata: The primary continuation itself marks Japan2/Korea1 deprecated and Adobe-KR added for PDF 2.0. Issue #5 on physical364 amends the preceding FD descriptor prose, not the Table123 collection/class names. Do not confuse these Table 123 names with the separate predefined-CMap compatibility obligations.
features.implementation_and_assertions: `pdf-font/src/glyph_class.rs` describes character-kind classification, collection-specific class inventories, ambiguous overlaps, and explicitly unclassifiable form/symbol classes. Unit tests assert Latin/digits/full-width Latin/Greek/Cyrillic/Kana/half-width Kana/ideograph/Hangul kinds; single-class membership, ambiguous Proportional+HRoman and Proportional+AlphaNum, the clause's Proportional+HKana example, and undecidable rotated/Ruby/Dingbats/Generic classes. `glyph_class_audit.rs::each_table_123_collection_row_recognizes_its_distinctive_character_classes` has a positive and cross-row negative for each of the six named collections (five physical rows), including added/deprecated collections. `loading.rs::a_glyph_class_descriptor_chooses_the_face_for_its_own_class_alone` exercises class-specific face application; public substitution choice remains dependent on available fonts.
features.verdict: Table 123's names and representative character descriptions have unusually broad unit coverage, and the class override has a separate consumer test. The tests do not raster-certify every class cell; they do directly cover each named collection with discriminating controls.
features.residuals: No public PDF fixture exercises every class name or every Unicode-to-class edge. Dingbats/Generic/rotated classes cannot be classified from Unicode character alone by this implementation and are refused with report; the source table descriptions do not supply an exact Unicode membership list for those categories. This is not a demonstrated reader defect.

features.table: Table 124 — Embedded font organisation for various font types
features.source_location: Caption and first rows physical 367 / printed 352; OpenType continuation physical 368 / printed 353. Table 125 starts later on physical 368 and is excluded. Table 124's OpenType row distinguishes the font dictionary kind and internal `glyf`/`CFF ` program form.

cells.program: TrueType; required core tables listed in the row.
OpenType with `glyf`, and the listed TrueType core tables.
OpenType with CID-keyed `CFF ` Top DICT operators; row also requires `cmap`.
OpenType with non-CID-keyed `CFF `; row also requires `cmap`.

features.ec3_and_errata: No effective issue annotation was found on Table 124's two physical pages. Table 124 itself gives the font-kind/program-format combinations and source table requirements; the detailed Type1/TrueType length fields belong to adjacent Table 125 and are intentionally not claimed here.
features.implementation_and_assertions: `crates/pdf-model/tests/opentype_selection_audit.rs` builds exact-xref PDFs and uses bundled CFF-OTF/glyf-TTF programs. Five tests assert literal selected glyph IDs for: name-keyed CFF in simple Type1; glyf in simple TrueType; name-keyed CFF in CIDFontType0; glyf in CIDFontType2; and the same compact CFF payload as Type1C. Each requested outline is also asserted nonempty. These are concrete consumer controls for the table's route choices, with fixture-provided real sfnt/CFF program bytes; they are not an independent ISO/IEC 14496-22 conformance validation. Other Type1/TrueType tests exercise the original FontFile and FontFile2 routes. The durable OpenType shard `font_dictionaries_current` is explicitly partial and also notes the non-exhaustive cross-product.
features.verdict: The principal format-selection branches in Table 124 have direct, differing expected glyph-index controls, including same-CFF comparison between OpenType and bare Type1C. This materially supports dispatch correctness; it is not full table conformance evidence.
features.residuals: No exhaustive valid profile spans every table/dictionary subtype combination or checks every required sfnt table family independently. Program conformance to the referenced font standards and malformed-program handling are outside this bounded cell audit. No additional test draft is warranted because current tests already distinguish the main dispatch branches; remaining cases are a validation/cross-product boundary rather than an observed wrong route.
